P5.detail: H agrees with G on 20 of 20

meaning.W: A work works if what it draws and labels is true to the 874 rows: each bridge stands where it really is and when it was really built, its colour matches its own rating, and its labels name the right things, so a reader is not misled about any column.
meaning.WT: A work works if it draws the 874 bridges faithfully to the record (positions in Delaware's real shape, years, lengths, traffic, ratings, counts and annotations all true to the CSV) and reads legibly, with no wrong facts, broken encodings or collided labels.

c1.P_why: Counts add to 874, county labels sit on their map bands, the callout points to a long arc, and the axis and the 1965-1969 peak match the drawing.
c1.W_why: The map, the counties, the legend counts (41/335/374/114/7/3) and the Delaware River callout (3,291 m, 1951) all agree with each other and with the data.
c1.WT_why: The map positions, colours, rating counts (41/335/374/114/7/3), 1965-69 peak of 88 and the Delaware River 3,291 m 1951 note all match the data, and the work reads clearly.
c1.G_why: The map keeps Delaware's shape with the county bands in place, and the 3,291 m 1951 bridge is labelled as crossing the Delaware River, which is right for the Delaware Memorial Bridge.
c1.H_why: The state's taper, the counties in order, the 3,291 m bridge of 1951 over the Delaware River in the far north: everything I know agrees.
c1.V_why: Checked the rating counts (41/335/374/114/7/3), '1965-1969: 88', the 5-year stack heights, the Delaware River 3,291 m 1951 label, the county counts and the map's shape.

c2.P_why: The poor-rating dots sit under red arcs and pair up at equal latitudes in both panels; the county labels and the latitude and year axes agree.
c2.W_why: It matches W15: correct geography, county labels, and consistent ratings and dots.
c2.WT_why: The latitudes, years, length widths (the C&D Canal spans show up as the large arches), colours and the ten rated-poor dots all match the record.
c2.G_why: It matches G08, with Delaware's outline intact and poor ratings only on older bridges.
c2.H_why: Indistinguishable for me from H11 (same dots, same outline); called real with no evidence either way.
c2.V_why: Checked all 10 rated-poor dots in both panels against latitude and year, the county counts (528/192/154), the earliest arches (1839, 1846, 1850, 1885) and the large rating-4 arch for the 2,570 m 1969 bridge.

c3.P_why: Legend counts add to 874, the oldest arc starts at 1839, arcs end at 2025, and the map is labelled correctly; nothing written contradicts the drawing.
c3.W_why: The map keeps Delaware's shape, the arcs' colours agree with when the poor bridges were built, and the legend totals add to 874.
c3.WT_why: The map has Delaware's true shape with correct rating colours, and the legend counts and the oldest bridge (1839, Brandywine Creek) are right.
c3.G_why: The map keeps Delaware's outline, the oldest 1839 bridge crosses Brandywine Creek, and the old wide arches are coloured as poorer than the recent ones.
c3.H_why: The bridges draw the state's outline (narrow north, broad Sussex), and the arches' colours match H03 and H09.
c3.V_why: Checked the rating counts (5/36/335/374/114/7/3), the oldest bridge (1839, Brandywine Creek), the arc colours by year (rating 4 in 1920, rating 3 in 1942) and the map's shape against the coordinates.

c4.P_why: Same layout as P02: the legend, river label, county labels and axis all agree with the drawing; nothing contradicts it.
c4.W_why: The map keeps Delaware's shape, the Delaware River crossing is labelled correctly, and the stacks by year carry plausible ratings (new bridges good, old ones mixed).
c4.WT_why: The positions, length widths, traffic weights and rating colours all agree with the record, and the year histogram and labels are correct and legible.
c4.G_why: It looks the same as G09, with the shape, the long red canal span and the age-related colour trend all as expected.
c4.H_why: Near-identical to H05; one of the two had its traffic dealt out and I cannot tell which.
c4.V_why: Checked the 5-year histogram heights and colours (all-blue 2018 stack of 31), the Delaware River 3,291 m label, the colour of the rating-4 2,570 m bridge and the map positions, which fit the coordinates to within about 1 px.

c1o1.P_why: Counts add to 874, the county labels are spread along the map, the callout points into the map, and the axis and the 1965-1969 peak agree.
c1o1.W_why: The map is stretched sideways out of Delaware's shape, and its callout points at the wrong place.
c1o1.WT_why: The map's positions are wrong (only about 560 of 874 bridges land where they really stand), so the state's shape is lost.
c1o1.G_why: The north of New Castle spreads across the full width instead of narrowing, so longitude was dealt out to the wrong bridges.
c1o1.H_why: Labels and the Delaware River note are right, but the map is as wide at the top as at the bottom, wider than H15's narrow north.
c1o1.V_why: The map's longitudes do not match the table: New Castle and Kent bridges are spread across the full width to the far east, where the coordinates put none.

c1o2.P_why: Rating counts add to 874, county counts 528/192/154 add to 874, and the county labels sit beside their bands of the map; the axis and the 1965-1969 callout match the tallest column.
c1o2.W_why: The 3,291 m 1951 Delaware River bridge is labelled 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem', a road name that does not belong to that crossing.
c1o2.WT_why: The note on the longest bridge (3,291 m, 1951) says it carries 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem' over nothing named, but that bridge crosses the Delaware River carrying I 295/US 40.
c1o2.G_why: It is the same as G01 except that the 3,291 m 1951 bridge is labelled as crossing 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem' instead of the Delaware River, so the crossing column was dealt out wrongly.
c1o2.H_why: Shape, county labels and timeline look right, but the longest bridge (3,291 m, 1951) is said to cross 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem' where its siblings H08, H10 and H15 say Delaware River; the 3,291 m bridge of 1951 is the Delaware Memorial Bridge, from memory.
c1o2.V_why: The 3,291 m, 1951 bridge is labelled 'Sr1/Korean War Vet Mem', but in the table it carries I 295 N & US 40 E over the Delaware River.

c1o3.P_why: The three county labels are stacked together at the top of the map, so Kent and Sussex label the same northern bridges as New Castle instead of their own bands.
c1o3.W_why: The map is out of shape, the county labels collide in one spot, and the Delaware River callout's leader line runs to a bridge in the middle of the state.
c1o3.WT_why: The map is distorted out of Delaware's shape, the three county labels overprint one another, and the Delaware River leader line points to the wrong place.
c1o3.G_why: The county labels have collapsed onto one latitude and the map is a scattered block, so the latitudes no longer belong to their bridges.
c1o3.H_why: The county labels collapse onto one another at the top, and the leader line from 'Delaware River' runs to an arch in the middle of the state rather than the north.
c1o3.V_why: The 'Delaware River 3,291 m, 1951' leader points to a glyph in the southern half of the map, but that bridge is at 39.69N in New Castle (the county labels are also piled together at the top).

c1a.P_why: The labels NEW CASTLE 528, KENT 192 and SUSSEX 154 are all printed on top of each other at one spot, so they label one part of the map as three different counties instead of marking three bands.
c1a.W_why: The map is distorted, the county labels overprint each other, the 3,291 m bridge is mislabelled 'Mispillion River, 1939', and the stack colours are reshuffled.
c1a.WT_why: It names the longest bridge 'Mispillion River, 1939', which is false, its county labels are printed on top of each other, and the map positions are wrong.
c1a.G_why: The 3,291 m bridge is said to cross the Mispillion River and to date from 1939, and the county labels have collapsed together.
c1a.H_why: The county labels collapse onto one another, and the 3,291 m bridge is said to cross the Mispillion River and be built in 1939; Delaware's longest bridge does not cross a small Kent river.
c1a.V_why: The 3,291 m bridge is labelled 'Mispillion River, 1939', but in the table the 3,290.6 m bridges cross the Delaware River and were built in 1951 and 1968.

c2o1.P_why: The legend says a dot marks a bridge rated poor (red), but many dots sit under blue and tan arcs (ratings 6-8), for example in the 1990s and 2018 blue clusters, rather than under the red arcs.
c2o1.W_why: The 'rated poor' dots sit on bridges coloured good and are placed differently from the other versions, so the dots and the ratings contradict each other.
c2o1.WT_why: The rated-poor dots are on the wrong bridges, including one on a bridge built around 2018, when no poor-rated bridge is newer than 1977.
c2o1.G_why: Its poor-rating dots sit at different years from G06/G08/G17, including bridges built around 1995 to 2018, which points to shuffled condition ratings.
c2o1.H_why: Outline and timeline match H11/H14, but the red 'rated poor' dots stand in other places on both halves, so the condition was dealt to other bridges.
c2o1.V_why: The rated-poor dots are in the wrong places: for example, the right panel has a dot at about 1992 and 39.66N, where the table has no poor bridge.

c2o2.P_why: Each poor-rating dot on the left sits at the same latitude as a dot on the right, and both dots sit under red arcs, as the subtitle and legend say; the county labels line up with latitude bands.
c2o2.W_why: The 'where' panel stretches the state into a rectangle, so the bridges are not drawn where they stand.
c2o2.WT_why: The 'where' map misplaces most bridges (Delaware's shape is lost, and the rated-poor dots disagree with the year panel).
c2o2.G_why: The 'where' map fills a rectangle with no narrow northern neck, so longitude is shuffled even though the year panel matches G08.
c2o2.H_why: The map's bridges spread evenly across the full width at every latitude; the state's outline is gone, while the timeline matches H11.
c2o2.V_why: The 'where' map has the wrong longitudes: the southernmost poor bridge (Assawoman Bay, SR 54, the most easterly in the table) is drawn mid-panel instead of at the eastern edge, and the map does not trace Delaware's shape.

c2o3.P_why: The poor-rating dots sit under red arcs and pair up at equal latitudes in both panels; the county labels sit beside their bands.
c2o3.W_why: The map has Delaware's shape, the counties sit in order north to south, and each poor dot falls on a red-rated arc at the same latitude in both panels.
c2o3.WT_why: The arch widths do not follow length: the 44 m 1839 bridge is drawn wide, while the 2,570 m C&D Canal bridge is tiny.
c2o3.G_why: The map has Delaware's shape, and the poor-rating dots fall only on bridges built before 1975, with the same dots on both sides.
c2o3.H_why: Shape, labels and red dots all agree with H14; one of the two had its lengths dealt out and I cannot see which.
c2o3.V_why: The arch widths do not follow length: the rated-poor 2,570 m C&D Canal bridge (1969, 39.56N) is drawn as a tiny arch.

c2a.P_why: SUSSEX 154, NEW CASTLE 528 and KENT 192 are all bunched around 39 deg 35'N (Sussex labelled north of New Castle), so they do not mark the latitude bands they claim; the dots themselves pair up correctly.
c2a.W_why: The 'where' panel is stretched into a rectangle and the county labels are in the wrong places (Sussex sits at the northern end).
c2a.WT_why: The 'where' panel is scrambled: the county labels are out of order and crowded together, and the bridges sit at the wrong latitudes (for example, the 1942 rated-poor dot falls near 39°15' instead of 39°43').
c2a.G_why: The county labels have collapsed together and the map has no Delaware outline, so latitude is shuffled.
c2a.H_why: The map has lost the state's shape and the county labels stand in the wrong order (Sussex above New Castle), which cannot happen if place and county belong together.
c2a.V_why: The county labels are stacked as Sussex, New Castle, Kent near 39.6N, but Sussex is the southernmost county (the poor-bridge dots are also misplaced).

c3o1.P_why: Legend counts add to 874, the oldest arc starts at 1839 and arcs end at 2025; no written item contradicts the drawing.
c3o1.W_why: The left-hand map is a rectangle of scattered bridges rather than Delaware, so the positions are false.
c3o1.WT_why: The map's bridge positions are scrambled into a rectangle, so it does not show where the bridges stand.
c3o1.G_why: The left map is a uniform rectangle instead of Delaware's outline, so longitude is shuffled.
c3o1.H_why: The outline is an even band from top to bottom, unlike H16 whose bridges draw the state's taper; the timeline matches H16, so place moved.
c3o1.V_why: The left map does not follow the coordinates: bridges are spread across a near-rectangle (for example, at the far east at New Castle latitudes) instead of tracing Delaware.

c3o2.P_why: Rating counts add to 874, the leftmost arc starts at 1839 as the 'oldest' line says, all arcs end at 2025, and about three pure-red rating-3 arcs are drawn.
c3o2.W_why: The colours are shuffled: compared with the correct versions, the poor-rated arcs have moved to recent bridges and the map has lost its fair and poor colours.
c3o2.WT_why: The map arches are coloured wrongly: under half of the isolated bridges match their rating, and the rating-4 C&D Canal bridge is drawn in the rating-3 red.
c3o2.G_why: The map matches G02, but the age arches lose the link between age and condition: the oldest arcs are grey and the red ones gather after 1965, so the years seem to be dealt out wrongly.
c3o2.H_why: The outline is right, but the arches' colours differ from H16's: red runs through the youngest arches, where the siblings are pale.
c3o2.V_why: The arc colours do not match the ratings: there is no rating-4 arc from 1920 or rating-3 arc from 1942, and the red arcs begin only in the 1960s.

c3o3.P_why: Legend counts add to 874, the oldest arc starts at 1839 and arcs end at 2025; no written item contradicts the drawing.
c3o3.W_why: The left-hand map spreads the bridges over a rectangle rather than the shape of Delaware, so 'each bridge where it stands' is not true.
c3o3.WT_why: The map scatters the bridges over a featureless rectangle that is not Delaware's real geography.
c3o3.G_why: The map is a rectangle with no Delaware outline, so longitude is shuffled.
c3o3.H_why: The map is an even-width band: the bridges keep their north-south density but not the state's outline; its timeline is H09's and H16's.
c3o3.V_why: The left map does not follow the table's coordinates: bridges at New Castle latitudes are spread out to the far eastern edge, so the outline of Delaware is lost.

c3a.P_why: Legend counts add to 874, the oldest arc starts at 1839, arcs end at 2025, and the number of red rating-3 arcs looks right; the left map's scattered placement cannot be checked against the page alone.
c3a.W_why: The caption says the oldest bridge, built 1839, crosses the SR 1 Milford bypass, a road far newer than the bridge, so the fields are mismatched; the map is also a rectangle.
c3a.WT_why: It says the oldest bridge crosses 'sr 1 milford bypass' (it crosses Brandywine Creek), and its map is not Delaware's shape.
c3a.G_why: The oldest bridge, built in 1839, is said to cross the SR 1 Milford Bypass, and the map is rectangular.
c3a.H_why: The oldest bridge, built 1839, is said to cross 'sr 1 milford bypass', a modern highway; and the map's outline is lost.
c3a.V_why: It says the oldest bridge (1839) crosses 'SR 1 Milford bypass', but the 1839 bridge in the table crosses Brandywine Creek.

c4o1.P_why: The legend colours appear in both panels, the river label sits beside a long arc, and the county labels and axis are consistent.
c4o1.W_why: The layout is the same as W03, but the ratings are attached to the wrong bridges: the newest bridges come out 'fair', the 1910s–40s bridges 'very good', and the Delaware River bridge changes colour.
c4o1.WT_why: The ratings are coloured wrongly: the rating-5 Delaware River bridge and the rating-4 C&D Canal bridge are drawn in the good-condition blues.
c4o1.G_why: The long canal span is grey-blue rather than red, and the colours in the year stacks differ from G09/G14 (the top of the 2018 stack is orange), so condition is shuffled.
c4o1.H_why: Map and labels hold, but the timeline's colours differ from H05/H18: the newest columns carry ochre caps where the siblings carry blue, so the ratings went to the wrong years.
c4o1.V_why: The colours are wrong: the 2018 stack (all rated 7-8 in the table) is drawn orange and tan, and the rating-5 Delaware River bridge is drawn blue.

c4o2.P_why: Legend colours match the arcs and the stacks, the delaware river label sits beside a long arc, and the county labels and the 1830-2030 axis line up with what is drawn.
c4o2.W_why: It matches W03: the geography, the labels and the per-bridge ratings all hold together.
c4o2.WT_why: The stroke weight does not follow traffic as its caption claims: roads with 44 vehicles a day are drawn as heavy as ones with 18,000.
c4o2.G_why: The map keeps its outline, the long red St. Georges-style span over the canal is in place, and the colours shift from orange for old bridges to blue for new ones.
c4o2.H_why: The map has the state's shape and the labels are in place; it is pixel-for-pixel close to H18 and I cannot tell which of the two had its traffic line-weights dealt out wrongly.
c4o2.V_why: The map glyphs' line weights do not follow ADT: some low-traffic bridges, such as 2418A418 with ADT 44, are drawn as heavily as busy ones (glyph weight barely correlates with traffic, unlike the correct rendering).

c4o3.P_why: The legend colours, the delaware river label beside a long arc, the county labels and the 1830-2030 stacked axis show no contradiction.
c4o3.W_why: The map is stretched far too wide for Delaware, so the bridges are not drawn where they stand, even though the year stacks are right.
c4o3.WT_why: The map's bridge positions are distorted into a rectangle that is not Delaware, so 'each drawn where it stands' is false.
c4o3.G_why: Very long arches turn up at small inland spots, such as a big red span east of the canal and large orange ones at the river label, so length is shuffled.
c4o3.H_why: The map is a rectangle of even width from top to bottom, not the state's narrow north and wide south; the timeline is the same as H05's and H18's, so only where the bridges stand moved.
c4o3.V_why: The map positions do not match the coordinates: bridges fill the whole width at every latitude, and the southern red (3-4) glyph sits mid-panel instead of at the eastern edge (Assawoman Bay).

c4a.P_why: The labels Kent, New Castle and Sussex are piled on top of each other at one height of the map, and the callout text overlaps the arcs, so they do not mark the county bands they name.
c4a.W_why: The map is a rectangle, the three county labels are piled on top of each other, and the long-bridge callout names a ramp instead of the Delaware River.
c4a.WT_why: The map loses Delaware's shape (bridges spread over a rectangle), and the county labels and the longest-bridge note pile on top of each other.
c4a.G_why: The county labels are piled together and the map is a scattered rectangle, so latitude and longitude are shuffled.
c4a.H_why: The longest bridge is said to be 'Kent ramp to 152', the county labels collapse together, and the map has lost the state's outline.
c4a.V_why: The county labels place Kent above New Castle and Sussex, all bunched at mid-height, but New Castle is the northernmost county in the table (and the 3,291 m bridge is labelled as a ramp rather than the Delaware River crossing).

P8.detail: scored by the practice from W's words, not blind: of W's 9 refusals in K, 5 name the state's shape the map should have, 2 a fact W holds about a named bridge or road, 2 a comparison with the other versions in the packet (one of them also: 'the newest bridges come out fair')

seatsnote: Each badge is one seat's verdict on that page. W and WT: does it work (W without the table, WT with it). Words: does every word on the page agree with its own drawing (P, no table). G and practice: real or dealt, told that some were dealt (green when right). V: does it agree with the table. The first picture of each row is the work as made; the other four are its dealt copies.
S146.PROMISE: falsified: K holds 11 pages; W refused 9 of them (the row falls at 6)
